text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout r-2026-03-15-73 has crossed abort thresholds (5xx rate > 8% over 3m). Service: inference-streaming, region: us-west-2. Paging on-call.

deploy-bot: Canary r-2026-03-15-73 -> image: inference:2026.03.15-rc3, feature flags: streaming-v2=on (20% canary). Healthchecks failing on 2/3 probes.

lee: on-call here. seeing pages. pulling metrics now. can someone drop grafana/gcloud traces?

jordan: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/canary-overview?orgId=1&from=now-15m&to=now : the 5xx spike lines up with the canary shift at +02:07. 5xx is primarily 504 gateway timeouts and 502s from runtime.

maria: support reports uptick in customer 504s for streaming sessions started after the deploy. support says affected customers are on streaming-v2 opt-in. tagging @support-jen for details.

jen: confirmed. Support triage: ~18 distinct customers reported degraded streaming start. No data loss but sessions fail to initialize ~50% of attempts for those customers. Ticket numbers 6571, 6572.

lee: quick assessment: impact is limited to opt-in streaming-v2 routes, but error rate for those routes is ~30% in the canary cohort. Abort criteria met. Recommend killing the streaming-v2 feature flag for all traffic in us-west-2 canary cohort, then rollback if needed.

tim: FYI I saw logs showing a new handshake timeout in the runtime: 
```
2026-03-15T14:07:11Z runtime[stream]: peer handshake failed: context deadline exceeded (ms: 120000)
2026-03-15T14:07:12Z proxy[http]: upstream response timeout after 60s -> 504
```
Seems like a mismatch of client timeouts and the new kernel path for streaming.

kyle: is this the quantized kernel switch? The canary image includes a kernel selection change that prefers async-kernel-v2 for streaming endpoints.

tim: yes. my local repro shows async-kernel-v2 can hang in certain payload sizes when prefix caching is warm. Not 100% sure.

lee: mitigation plan: 1) flip streaming-v2 feature flag off for canary cohort in us-west-2, 2) observe error rate drop, 3) if still bad, roll back canary image. I'm executing 1 now.

maria: please run the flag flip via flags service and post command/output. Keep me posted on customer comms.

lee: running internal CLI: 
```
# flip flag for canary cohort (us-west-2)
redwood-ff set streaming-v2 --cohort canary-usw2 --value false --reason "abort-canary-1855"
```

deploy-bot: Action accepted. Change queued: ff-change-id=ff-8942, target=canary-usw2, value=false. Expect prop to take ~30s.

incident-bot: :information_source: FLAG_CHANGE: ff-8942 applied by lee at 2026-03-15T14:09:10Z. Audited.

lee: flag is reported as false across the canary instances. Watching metrics.

jordan: 5xx rate for canary routes dropping: was 31% -> now 7.6% (1m window). Latency still elevated but error reduction looks good.

maria: support: starting to update customer tickets with mitigation steps. Will send an outbound note if errors persist after 15m.

tim: remote logs show fewer handshake timeouts now. Some leftover 504s due to in-flight requests.

lee: summary at +10m: flipping the flag reduced 5xx to below abort threshold but latency for some requests still ~30% higher than baseline. I recommend rolling back the canary image to inference:2026.03.14-stable to remove kernel change entirely. Thoughts?

kyle: rollback is sensible. We should avoid full region redeploy; do canary abort + revert to stable canary image and stop traffic shift. deploy-bot, can you abort canary rollout and set canary image to stable?

deploy-bot: Initiating canary abort: rollback to image inference:2026.03.14-stable for r-2026-03-15-73. Steps: 1) stop traffic shift, 2) redeploy canary instances with stable image, 3) verify healthchecks. Confirm to proceed.

lee: proceed. execute now.

deploy-bot: 
```
# abort canary
deployctl abort --rollout r-2026-03-15-73 --reason "canary-abort-1855" && 
deployctl set-image --rollout r-2026-03-15-73 --image inference:2026.03.14-stable && 
deployctl resume --rollout r-2026-03-15-73
```

incident-bot: :rocket: Deployment actions started by deploy-bot at 2026-03-15T14:14:02Z. Keep eyes on healthchecks.

jordan: healthchecks trending: canary instances cycling, new pods coming up with stable image. Initial probes passing. 5xx for canary cohort down to 1.2% in last 2m.

tim: verifying logs on new instances: no handshake timeout traces in the stable image. Good.

lee: confirming customer impact assessment: affected cohort ~20% of traffic, but only customers who opted into streaming-v2 (opt-in). Estimating ~0.8% of total active accounts saw failures during the 12-minute window. No data corruption, no persistent queues stalled.

maria: support update: sending follow-up to affected accounts with apology and mitigation summary. Also opening SAF ticket to offer credits for impacted sessions.

jen: sending initial outbound now. Will CC incident channel with draft.

lee: post-mitigation checklist: 1) confirm stable image health for 30m, 2) keep streaming-v2 flag off for all regions until investigation complete, 3) spawn a P0 postmortem with eng-runtime, oncall, and product.

kyle: allocating runtime eng: @sophia will lead the kernel regression triage. Sophia, can you take ownership?

sophia: taking. I'll start with a bisect between async-kernel-v1 and v2 on our repro and examine handshake codepaths. Creating issue in repo: runtime/infra#4109.

lee: handoff: my shift ends in 25m. On-call for next shift will be jordan. Jordan, please pick up monitoring for the next hour and start the postmortem draft when stable.

jordan: acknowledged. I'll keep watching for 60m and start the postmortem doc. I'll include timeline, flags, rollout metadata, and customer impact.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: RESOLVED on-call action: canary aborted and rolled back at 2026-03-15T14:17:35Z. Follow-up: postmortem required.

lee: adding quick RCA notes: probable kernel path regression in async-kernel-v2 causing handshake timeouts under certain prefix-caching states. Root cause TBD.

tim: saving logs / traces to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1855-canary-abort/ for triage.

maria: creating customer incident record and linking tickets -> INC-1855. Also scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

jen: draft outbound done. Sending in 5 mins after I sync with product.

lee: final: thanks everyone. If anything flares, page me. Leaving handoff notes in #oncall-handoff.

jordan: taking over. will update if anything changes.

sophia: started bisect job. first results in ~45m.

incident-bot: :memo: Thread closed for active mitigation. All actions and flag changes are auditable under ff-8942 and deploy action ids recorded.
